intent: Collect a fixed-length one-time code, one character per slot, as one string value.
typical_uses: A verification or one-time passcode of a known, fixed length

dont_use_when.situation: A short free-form value whose length varies (a promo code, a postal code), or a single numeric value such as an amount or a quantity

instead.note: Input, with `type="number"` or `inputMode="numeric"` for a number; InputOtp splits its value into one slot per character and only completes once every slot is filled.

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

Every value, whether given through `value`, `defaultValue` or typed and pasted, is stripped of whitespace, filtered by `validationType`, passed through `normalizeValue` and clamped to `length` characters before the slots show it.

`id` is not rendered on the root element: the first slot receives it and each later slot receives `{id}-2`, `{id}-3` and so on. A `<label htmlFor>` naming that `id` therefore labels the first slot. Unless the root is given its own `aria-labelledby`, the primitive then points the root's and every slot's `aria-labelledby` at that label; a slot given its own `aria-labelledby`, or a slot other than the first given its own `aria-label`, keeps that instead.

anti_patterns.dont: Label the field with `aria-label` on the first slot
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put a Label whose `htmlFor` names the root's `id` - the primitive drops `aria-label` from the first slot and warns in development when that slot has no associated label

anti_patterns.dont: Render a number of InputOtpSlot parts that differs from `length`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render exactly `length` slots - the value is clamped to `length`, not to the slots rendered, completion fires only at `length` characters, and the primitive warns in development when the two counts differ

a11y.by: The primitive's OTPField.Root (role="group", aria-labelledby taken from a label associated with the first slot) and OTPField.Input (focus moved between slots by the arrow, Home and End keys) plus input-otp.test.tsx's assertion that typing into the first slot moves focus to the second

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a function called with the next code string and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape, whose reason names what changed the value (typing, clearing, pasting or a key), which only tsc can check.

onValueComplete.states: onValueComplete is a function called with the full code string once every slot is filled, not a value
onValueComplete.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. It also fires when a complete value is pasted over an already complete one, and runs right before the owning form is submitted when `autoSubmit` is on.

onValueInvalid.states: onValueInvalid is a function called with the attempted text when validation or normalization rejects characters, not a value
onValueInvalid.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its first argument is the raw text the user typed or pasted, before normalization.

normalizeValue.states: normalizeValue is a function from a string to a string, applied after whitespace and validationType filtering
normalizeValue.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its result is filtered by `validationType` again and clamped to `length`, and it may run more than once on the same value, so it has to be idempotent.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the field's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the field's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (complete, disabled, readOnly, required, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through input-otp.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: OTPField.Root renders one extra native input beside the root element, hidden from assistive tech and out of the tab order, that carries the whole code for `name`, `form`, `required` and constraint validation; the kit exports no part for it.

good.title: Six digits in two groups, labelled by a sibling Label

bad.title: Four slots under a length of six
bad.why: A pasted six-character code is accepted in full while only four characters are visible, and completion needs six characters the user can never type into the missing slots.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. normalizeValue is a function from a string to a string, applied after whitespace and validationType filtering.
